findings.title: English file path derivation breaks for non-community/any path and regex is wrong
findings.body: The English counterpart is derived by replacing 'resources-community' with 'resources' and then replacing the regex `_[a-zA-Z-_]*\.properties` with `_en.properties`. The regex also matches any underscore in the directory path (e.g. under a path containing '_'), and `[a-zA-Z-_]*` is greedy across the filename. For files without a locale suffix (e.g. base files, or paths with underscores in directory names such as 'keycloak_theme/'), the replacement corrupts the path and `new FileInputStream(englishFile)` throws, which is wrapped in a RuntimeException that aborts verification of the whole module rather than reporting a message.

findings.title: Verifier throws RuntimeException on missing English file instead of reporting
findings.body: When the translated file has no corresponding English file (or the path derivation fails), verifySafeHtml throws a RuntimeException. The verify() method only catches IOException, so this propagates as an unchecked failure that aborts the entire Maven plugin run instead of adding a message to the result list. Also the English file is read even when the file being checked is itself the English file (for _en files the replacement is a no-op, so it compares a file to itself, which is harmless but masks the case).

findings.title: Missing translation keys are silently treated as empty English source
findings.body: getEnglishValue returns "" when a key is absent in the English bundle. containsHtml("") is then false, so a translation for a key that does not exist in English is checked with the no-HTML policy and any HTML in it is reported, while keys that legitimately contain HTML in English but were removed or renamed in English are not detected. Missing source keys should be reported explicitly.

findings.title: Message string built from substring indexes can throw
findings.body: The diff-highlighting computes `start` and `end` independently. When the value and sanitized strings overlap (e.g. one is a prefix of the other or the common prefix and suffix overlap), `value.substring(start, value.length() - end)` can have start > end, throwing StringIndexOutOfBoundsException and aborting the verifier. For example value='<b>x' vs sanitized='x' overlaps can produce this.

findings.title: Anchor replacement removes first occurrence anywhere, not at its position
findings.body: santizeAnchors uses value.replaceFirst(Pattern.quote(englishMatcher.group()), "") which removes the first textual occurrence of the anchor tag, and the loop matches tags in the translated value against English tags by order only. A translation with a changed/extra anchor whose text coincidentally matches an earlier English tag can be silently accepted, and the matcher positions are not updated after the string is modified, so matching continues over a stale string. The `break` after reporting also means only one anchor error is reported per key.

findings.title: Tests rely on fixture paths whose English counterparts do not exist in the test resources
findings.body: verifySafeHtml derives the English file by replacing the locale suffix with _en.properties in the same directory. Fixtures such as noHtml_de.properties and changedAnchor_de.properties rely on noHtml_en.properties and changedAnchor_en.properties existing; this works, but illegalHtmlTag_en.properties is verified against itself, so the test for illegal HTML only passes because of the English HTML being the same as the translation. The tests also do not assert the absence of false positives (e.g. a valid translation producing no messages), so the sanitizer's acceptance behaviour is untested.

findings.title: Illegal-HTML fixture is a malformed English source rather than a translation
findings.body: The fixture `key=Some <div>tag</div` is an unterminated tag in the English reference file itself, and the test asserts 'Illegal HTML' for it. The fixture does not exercise a translation containing disallowed HTML versus an English source, so the test does not verify the intended rule that a translation may not introduce tags absent from the source.

findings.title: Renamed fixture and weakened assertion
findings.body: The duplicate-keys test was changed from Matchers.contains to Matchers.hasItem, so it no longer asserts the exact message list; any extra spurious message would now pass. Combined with the new verifySafeHtml running for duplicateKeys_en.properties, this weakens the regression coverage for the existing check.

findings.title: Finnish translation replaced with a different, untranslated-language sentence
findings.body: The `totpStep1` key was rewritten to a generic Finnish sentence without the links to the authenticator apps, dropping information present in the source. This is an unrelated content change to a translation, not a sanitizer fix, and removes the app names users need.

findings.title: Lithuanian totpStep1 replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The value `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian, not Lithuanian. It will be shown to Lithuanian users in the account console and also drops the FreeOTP/Google Authenticator links that the translation previously contained.

findings.title: Lithuanian loginTotpStep1 replaced with Italian text
findings.body: `loginTotpStep1=Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` is Italian copied into the Lithuanian login bundle, so Lithuanian users see the wrong language and the links to the authenticator apps are removed.

findings.title: Lithuanian email HTML hrefs now quoted but placeholders inconsistent
findings.body: The HTML email bodies were changed to use `<a href="{0}">` and the identityProviderLinkBodyHtml/passwordReset links now use `{3}` and `{0}` respectively, while the text body uses `{4}` for the expiry. Changing placeholder usage in translations without checking argument order against the English source risks wrong values (e.g. expiry shown as link) in the sent emails.

findings.body: The emailVerificationBodyHtml line previously had `` (a broken tag); the diff corrects it, but the rest of the file was not touched, while the same file also still contains the malformed-looking unchanged content elsewhere. The change is only a partial cleanup of the markup, leaving the translation's HTML inconsistent with the sanitizer's rules.

findings.title: Hungarian emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml key prefixed with *** garbage
findings.body: The diff shows the line starting with `***emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml=` in the removed side; the replacement line is correct, but the removal of the stray prefix indicates an accidental edit that must be verified so that the key is actually emailUpdateConfirmationBodyHtml in the final file.

findings.title: Multiple WebAuthn br tag changes are whitespace-only churn
findings.body:
The `
` to `
` changes across many locales are cosmetic and unrelated to the sanitizer, adding diff noise to ~40 translation files; they do not fix any verifier failure described in the PR.

findings.title: Slovak error-invalid-multivalued-size placeholder changed to a non-plural choice with wrong index
findings.body: The fix changes the second choice placeholder from {1,choice,...} to {2,choice,...} while leaving the same message elsewhere; the new value uses four-plural forms with a choice pattern whose thresholds (4<hodnôt) are inconsistent with the English pattern used in other locales, so plural rendering for counts 2–4 may be wrong.

findings.title: Czech error-invalid-multivalued-size choice pattern differs from English source placeholders
findings.body: The Czech value uses `{1,choice,...}` and `{2,choice,...}` with 1<hodnoty|4<hodnot patterns while the English source has `{2,choice,...}` only; it is inconsistent with the key's intended single-count phrasing and the verifier's normalizeValue only strips choice patterns for specific keys, so this key may be flagged or render incorrectly.

findings.title: English error-invalid-multivalued-size choice changed but other locales keep old placeholders
findings.body: The base English message now uses a choice format for {2}, while many translations keep the plain `value(s)` form or use `{1,choice}` on the wrong index; the inconsistent placeholder sets between source and translations can cause MessageFormat to render differently per locale and the verifier's normalization only covers the admin key.
